sense: what something rests on, its grounds

terms.gloss: the foundation, the basis (of a virtue, an argument, a life)
evidence: Cic. Planc. 29: pietās fundāmentum est omnium virtūtum
Cic. Off. 1.23: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs
terms.comment: Of buildings usually plural (see foundations); of virtues, arguments and plans in either number: jacere pācis fundāmenta, to lay the basis of peace (Cic. Phil. 1.1, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: rest on, be based on, rely on
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent; with in and the ablative, or the ablative alone
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.55: conjectūra omnis, in quā nītitur dīvīnātiō
Cic. Off. 1.122: quōrum cōnsiliō atque auctōritāte nītātur
terms.comment: “X is based on Y”: X in Y nītitur. Lewis & Short: “to rest, rely, depend upon a thing”.

terms.gloss: on the basis of, according to, from
evidence: Traupman 92: Ex verbīs tuīs colligō, I infer from what you say
terms.comment: What a conclusion or a claim rests on: ex tuīs litterīs, on the strength of your letter.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.38: eadem causa subest (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a cause, a reason or a suspicion that lies behind something: causa subest (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: mementōte eam mē senectūtem laudāre, quae fundāmentīs adulēscentiae cōnstitūta sit
phrases.english: remember that the old age I praise is one built on the foundations laid in youth
dutiful love is the basis of all the virtues

phrases.latin: Jam teneō. Ex verbīs tuīs colligō tē pecūniam magis quam cōnsilium ā mē petere.
phrases.english: Now I get it. I gather from what you say that you are asking me for money rather than advice.

sources: Lewis & Short: fundamentum · Lewis & Short: nitor · Lewis & Short: ex · Lewis & Short: subsum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 92.
Cicero, Pro Plancio, De officiis 1, De divinatione 2 and De senectute, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
